overview: The Philippines is an island country in South-East Asia, made up of more than 7,000 islands in the western Pacific. Its capital is Manila, part of the huge Metro Manila area. The Philippines was a Spanish colony for more than 300 years and then an American territory, becoming independent in 1946. Filipino and English are its official languages, and most Filipinos are Christian.

geography.text: The islands fall into three main groups: Luzon in the north, the Visayas in the middle and Mindanao in the south. Most are mountainous and volcanic, with active volcanoes such as Mayon and Taal. The Philippines lies on the Pacific Ring of Fire and in the path of typhoons, and its seas have some of the richest coral reefs in the world.

history.text: Ferdinand Magellan's expedition reached the islands in 1521, and Spain ruled them for more than 300 years, naming them after King Philip II. After the Philippine Revolution of 1896 and the Spanish–American War, the United States took control. The Philippines became independent in 1946, and the 'People Power' revolution of 1986 peacefully removed the dictator Ferdinand Marcos.

events.title: Magellan arrives
events.text: Magellan's expedition reaches the islands; he is killed at Mactan.

events.title: Spanish colony
events.text: Spain begins its colonisation of the islands.

events.title: US rule
events.text: Spain gives the Philippines to the United States.

events.title: People Power
events.text: Peaceful protests end the Marcos dictatorship.
